questions.question: Cpu ram
questions.answer: Linux systemd 253+ scopes set terminal CPUWeight=10 (active terminal 100) and OOMPolicy=continue; absent a usable user bus, they are unavailable. macOS/Windows lower process priority; macOS cannot raise nice back without root.

questions.question: Cancellation
questions.answer: Close ends the terminal and tracked processes. Linux without a user bus and macOS detached processes whose environment cannot be inspected can outlive it; already-running external browser apps also remain.

questions.question: Fairness

questions.question: Recovery
questions.answer: No scheduler, queues or shared check reuse.

limitations: No job queue, resource admission scheduler or shared test-result cache. Linux scopes require systemd 253+ and a user bus; processes outside a terminal scope are not protected by it. Detached-process cleanup has platform exceptions.

questions.answer: Feedback notes and uninstall goodbye answers kept 12 months; nightly AI feedback themes at most two months; tour ticket rows 90 days.

questions.answer: Feedback notes and goodbye answers cannot be deleted on request because they are anonymous; local data deleted at uninstall when unticked.

questions.question: Training
questions.answer: Each night an AI model sorts the last month of feedback notes into themes through OpenRouter, only to providers that do not train; goodbye answers are not sent to it; the tour asks zero retention.

questions.answer: Local data; novadeck.dev services run on Cloudflare, and US processors may handle requests outside the EU.

questions.question: Telemetry disclosure
questions.answer: Privacy page lists update-check fields and counts.

questions.question: Telemetry default
questions.answer: On by default in the installed desktop app. The README badge says no telemetry and no update check sends a per-install ID, but packaged builds check novadeck.dev 10 seconds after launch and then hourly with their version and build, and the website counts each check; the privacy page says it counts copies open each hour by channel and system and launches each day by version, build and country. Crash dumps stay local. Local, pull request and development builds make no checks.

questions.question: Telemetry controls
questions.answer: NOVADECK_UPDATES=off turns update checks off for a launch; there is no Preferences switch, and feedback notes send only on Send.

questions.question: Telemetry off switch location
questions.answer: Config only: launching the desktop app with the NOVADECK_UPDATES=off environment variable turns off its update checks, and with them the counted requests, for that launch. Preferences has no update-check or telemetry switch; its Experimental switch only picks the release channel.

questions.question: Consent prompt
questions.answer: Feedback notes send only on Send and uninstall goodbye answers only on a click; the tour asks for a ticket. The goodbye page is described on the privacy page but absent from pinned 8dd943a.

questions.question: Provider separation
questions.answer: Agents talk to their own providers directly.

limitations: Update checks are on in installed builds; only the NOVADECK_UPDATES=off environment variable turns them off, and Preferences has no switch for them.

claims.answer: Free with no paid plan; agent usage is billed by each harness vendor.

sources.title: Novadeck README
sources.finding: Desktop terminal for Claude Code, Codex, Antigravity, opencode and pi; one Inbox for agent questions; free and open source with no account; runs the CLIs the person already has with their own accounts; macOS, Windows and Linux installers.

sources.title: Using Novadeck guide
sources.locator: Connect your agents, Three views, The Inbox, Teams, After a restart
sources.finding: Welcome dialog installs a small plugin into each ticked agent; Focus, Grid and Canvas views; Inbox for permissions, plans and questions with toasts and system notifications; agents message each other by handle and lead teammates; terminals reopen after restart and closed ones stay in History.

sources.title: Novadeck reference: Install
sources.finding: macOS universal dmg/install script, Windows x64 per-user installer and ZIP, Linux x86_64 AppImage; optional AppArmor profile for the Electron sandbox; uninstall keeps projects unless unticked; installed builds auto-update and never restart by themselves.

sources.title: Novadeck reference: Working in Novadeck
sources.locator: lines 79-562 (views, Agent Chat, notifications, projects, Inbox, sessions)
sources.finding: Project switcher shows per-project agent state (working, paused at usage limit, waiting); Inbox lists Unblock, Question, Trouble and Update rows that stay as gray history; desktop system notifications per agent finish or error; projects can be pinned, reordered and removed; sessions group terminals; browser build shows no notifications.

sources.title: Novadeck reference: History
sources.locator: History introduction lines 565-567 and conflicting Closing asks first paragraph lines 608-610; implementation cross-check in backend/runner/src/terminals/history.ts lines 38 and 524-536
sources.finding: The History introduction says closed terminals can be restored for 7 days; the Closing asks first paragraph in the same section still says 30 days. The pinned implementation uses 7 days.

sources.title: Novadeck reference: Restoring terminals
sources.locator: lines 626-773 (shell integration, connecting agents, transcripts, permissions)
sources.finding: After reboot each terminal reopens in its folder and connected agents resume their sessions; connecting installs a Novadeck plugin (hooks and MCP) into each harness; transcripts are masked for secrets and encrypted with an OS keychain key; Claude Code is allowed only Novadeck MCP tools by flag, other permissions stay the harness own.

sources.title: Agent messaging: Agent interface
sources.finding: Inside Novadeck terminals agents get MCP tools send, show, look, open_terminal, open_agent, close_terminal, lead and release, plus worktree tools when enabled; send answers queued, held or refused and never claims delivery.

sources.title: Agent messaging: Herd, Solo and Swarm
sources.finding: Preference picks how far agents act on each other: Herd (default) lets agents settle overlaps directly; Solo and Swarm sit behind an experimental switch; Swarm lets agents open, lead and close teammates without asking.

sources.title: Agent messaging: The shipping gate
sources.finding: Experimental, off by default: gates gh pr create, gh pr merge and pushes or ref moves outside the agent own worktree branch behind an Inbox permit; only exact commands a live permit covers are allowed.

sources.title: Agent workspace: Worktrees
sources.finding: Experimental agent worktrees (Preferences, Experimental, off by default): open_worktree, take_worktree, close_worktree, give_worktree create and track git worktrees under ~/.novadeck/worktrees with owner terminal, branch and base recorded; the Worktrees panel measures each against its home branch.

sources.title: runner worktrees repo.ts
sources.finding: Runner runs git worktree add to create an agent worktree for a branch.

sources.title: runner shipping reader.ts
sources.locator: header comment and permit keys, lines 1-95
sources.finding: Shipping targets are gh pr create, gh pr merge (with separate --auto and --admin targets) and pushes or ref moves; permits are keyed by repository and branch or PR number.

sources.title: @novadeck/forges README
sources.finding: Finds the pull request of a git branch on GitHub, GitLab and Azure DevOps using the signed-in gh, glab or az token; stores no secret.

sources.title: Backend API: Running a standalone runner
sources.finding: Standalone runner keeps workspace.sqlite and transcripts in a data folder, can run under systemd or Docker on a VPS behind a TLS reverse proxy; there is no TLS, login page or public multi-user hosting layer.

sources.title: Backend API: Serving a runner and Devices
sources.finding: Runner serves token-authenticated WebSockets at /api/rpc; owner token NOVADECK_TOKEN plus per-device credentials the owner mints and revokes; a device has the same shell access as the owner.

sources.title: Harness adapters: Shims and the worktrees folder
sources.finding: Each connected harness gets a shim; Claude Code receives the worktrees folder through its settings and Codex as writable roots, under the person own permission mode or sandbox; Novadeck writes nothing to harness config.

sources.title: Harness adapters: Usage, quota resets and context
sources.finding: Design for usage, limit windows and context per harness: limits stored as used fraction with reported reset; estimates labelled; account access stays inside adapters.

sources.title: TerminalTab.tsx usage-limit display
sources.finding: Terminal tab shows an agent paused at its usage limit with the reset time.

sources.title: Harness coverage matrix
sources.finding: Per-harness coverage of hooks, resume, messaging and status for Claude Code, Codex, Antigravity, opencode and pi.

sources.title: Novadeck LICENSE
sources.finding: GNU GPL version 3; README states GPL-3.0-or-later with contributions under a CLA.

sources.title: apps/desktop package.json
sources.finding: Desktop app is Electron with a React 19 renderer.

sources.title: Novadeck home page
sources.finding: Desktop terminal for Claude Code, Codex, Antigravity on existing subscriptions; operatingSystem macOS, Windows, Linux; isAccessibleForFree true; offer price 0 USD; GPL-3.0.

sources.title: Download Novadeck
sources.finding: Costs nothing and asks for nothing; on a phone the page says Novadeck is a desktop app and offers to send the link to a computer.

sources.title: Novadeck privacy
sources.locator: What the app sends; onboarding tour; What the site counts (last changed 2026-11-23)
sources.finding: No account or telemetry ID; the app sends no code, terminals, chats or logs except during the onboarding tour, which runs agents on Novadeck OpenRouter account via Azure with zero retention requested; update checks send version and build and are counted by country; feedback notes are anonymous and kept 12 months.

sources.title: Novadeck GitHub releases
sources.finding: v1.12.15 prerelease 2026-11-25; latest stable v1.11.63 2026-11-24; several releases per day.

sources.title: Novadeck GitHub issues
sources.finding: Public issues track bugs and requests such as multi-window support (#1107) and a Windows shipping-gate gap (#1206); no dated roadmap.

sources.title: GitHub API repository record
sources.finding: 60 stars on 2026-11-25; repository created 2026-09-19.

sources.title: Timing bench README
sources.finding: Timing run drives the production web UI in headless Chromium against a real runner with fake agents sending hooks and status-line telemetry; numbers are a trend, too noisy to gate on.

sources.title: Bounded search: container or VM isolation
sources.locator: grep -riE "devcontainer|docker run|podman" in backend, frontend, harnesses, apps, libraries, docs
sources.finding: Only two hits, both shell-command display helpers; no container or VM runtime for agents. Docker appears only as a way to host the standalone runner.

sources.title: Bounded search: issue tracker and planning
sources.locator: grep -riE "linear.app|jira|gh issue" and review of backend/runner/src module list (no issues, tasks or backlog module)
sources.finding: No issue store, backlog, Linear or Jira integration; units of work are terminals, sessions, projects and worktrees.

sources.title: Bounded search: SSO and roles
sources.finding: Only a test fixture string and demo data match; no SSO, organisations or roles. Access is the runner owner token plus device credentials.

sources.title: Bounded search: cost tracking
sources.finding: Matches are message rate limits and trouble rows; no per-task or per-session dollar cost display.

sources.title: Bounded search: schedules and triggers
sources.locator: grep -riE "cron|schedul" in source; reviewed hits in forges/service.ts, terminals/active.ts, harnesses/activity.ts
sources.finding: Hits are internal polling and agent self wake-ups; no user-facing schedules, recurring tasks or event triggers.

sources.title: Bounded search: other clients
sources.locator: apps/ holds desktop, previews and try only; no react-native, expo or capacitor dependency in apps/*/package.json; no editor-extension package
sources.finding: No mobile app or editor extension; apps/try is a browser demo and the browser build is a development target.

sources.title: Novadeck MCP tools (shell/mcp.ts)
sources.locator: header comment lines 14-17; model and effort properties lines 539-565
sources.finding: open_agent opens a terminal running another connected harness, on a model and effort when asked, with a brief as its task; the runner lists each harness's models and efforts.

sources.title: Novadeck SubscriptionUsage footer component
sources.locator: WindowRow and UsageDetail, lines 30-60; mounted in frontend/ui/src/app/FooterSection.tsx line 368
sources.finding: The footer shows each connected agent subscription with its usage windows as bars, the used share and when each window resets, as the agent reports them.

sources.title: Novadeck agentStats (frontend/core/src/agents/stats.ts)
sources.locator: AgentStats type and agentStats, lines 14-45; rendered by frontend/ui/src/app/WorkspaceTerminal.tsx line 230
sources.finding: Each agent terminal window shows the model, effort and how full its context is, as a share or as tokens held; these are live readings, not totals or statistics.

sources.title: Novadeck auto-update design
sources.finding: Setting NOVADECK_UPDATES=off turns update checks off for a launch; the Preferences Updates section has only the Experimental channel switch, no update-check switch.

sources.title: Novadeck runner source search for retries, run limits and traces
sources.locator: rg -ni 'retr(y|ies)|timeout|max_?turns|trace|statistic|usage.{0,20}export' across backend/runner/src, harnesses and frontend, with production hits inspected separately from test/spec fixtures
sources.finding: No agent run-time or turn cap, usage export or aggregate statistics module was found in the scoped implementation. Retry paths handle delivery/files/engine operations, not rerunning failed agent turns. Production doorbell tracing exists in messaging/doorbell-log.ts and is wired by apps/desktop/src/runner/index.ts; it is not only test code.

sources.title: Novadeck plan editor
sources.finding: The companion plan pane edits file plans and notes and highlights the latest rewrite. Transcript plans are read-only; unsaved changes can be lost when the pane closes. Revision stamps support conflict handling, not an immutable plan history.

sources.title: Novadeck plan save
sources.finding: File plans are reread from disk. Save compares the source stamp, limits editing to regular plan files inside project or harness plan folders, caps at 256 KiB, and renames a temporary file over the original. Transcript plans remain read-only.

sources.title: Novadeck plan store
sources.locator: items/saveItem lines 3003-3080; companions/records.ts ItemRecord; companions/items.ts planObserved/observe
sources.finding: SQLite companion_items stores a plan pointer with stable item id, path, agent/session and format. It is not a copy or acceptance-criteria/task model. Surviving pointers reread file or transcript content; loss of source makes the item unavailable.

sources.title: Novadeck doorbell traces
sources.locator: createDoorbellLog lines 49-135; logDoorbell lines 181-197; wired in apps/desktop/src/runner/index.ts line 53
sources.finding: Production tracing keeps the latest 100 decision lines per terminal in memory, logs them on ring failure or after messages wait five minutes, and emits debug trace lines. Verbose mode also logs selected screen rows. This is a diagnostic log, not an end-to-end task trace viewer.

sources.title: Novadeck open budgets
sources.locator: New terminals lines 880-900; docs/agent-messaging.md Agent interface; backend/runner/src/messaging/send-rates.ts
sources.finding: The runner limits opening to five terminals or fifteen led teammates per minute from a shared initiating chain budget, and twenty per minute runner-wide. Messaging has separate sender/pair/runner limits and holds idle loops; these are not token, dollar or agent-run deadlines.

sources.title: Novadeck desktop update checks at commit 8dd943a
sources.locator: apps/desktop/src/main/updates/updater.ts lines 26-30 (first check 10 s after launch, then hourly, each counted on novadeck.dev), 44-54 (CheckFacts: version and installed/portable build so the website can count active copies), 123-130 (checkHeaders), 193-203 (updaterKind; looksForUpdates requires a packaged nonzero version and NOVADECK_UPDATES not off); apps/desktop/src/main/index.ts line 187 (crashReporter uploadToServer false)
sources.finding: Packaged builds with a real version check novadeck.dev for updates 10 seconds after launch and then hourly, adding the check reason, version and installed or portable build so the website can count active copies. A launch with NOVADECK_UPDATES=off makes no checks. Native crash dumps are kept locally and never uploaded.

sources.title: Novadeck auto-update design: what a check sends and how the website counts it
sources.finding: Update checks read novadeck.dev, which counts each request to know how many copies are open and launched, then answers with the release file from GitHub. A check adds only its reason, version and build, and the per-install staging ID is patched out; the requested file name still reveals the system. Windows, macOS and Linux AppImage builds check; local, pull request and development builds do not.

sources.title: Novadeck privacy (last changed 25 November 2026)
sources.locator: What the app sends; feedback card; uninstall goodbye page; nightly AI sorting; onboarding tour; Who else sees your requests; Why, and who to ask
sources.finding: The app sends no code, terminals, chats or logs except during the onboarding tour. Update checks send reason, version and build with no ID; the site keeps only the country and counts copies open each hour by channel and system and launches each day by version, build and country. Feedback notes are sent only on Send; the uninstaller opens a goodbye page whose answers are kept only when clicked. Both are anonymous, kept 12 months and cannot be deleted on request. Each night an AI model sorts the last month of notes into themes through OpenRouter, only to providers that do not train; themes are kept at most two months. Tour ticket rows are deleted after 90 days. Cloudflare, GitHub, OpenRouter, Microsoft Azure and Hugging Face are named; requests may be handled outside the EU.
